x: The next race was the 2 miles Team Race, 3 aside, all to count. Burt, Johnson and Ross represented the L.A C, and J.

The two men referred to (Burt and Hancock) scored between them 36 of our rivals' 117 points. Burt used to be a prominent distance runner in the Blackheath Harriers ranks; while Hancock was running over the country less than a year ago, but now appears to be a Walking Champion in embryo.

The Surrey Walking Club men have a habit of producing their best walking soon after six miles, but although Hake and Burt walked very strongly over the last part of the journey and picked up many valuable points, they could not get up to our leaders.

Hake (S.W.C.) who had shown very fast time in the Stock Exchange Championship, was second, and Burt, of the same Club, third. Brown, of ours, showed splendid form in finishing fourth and during the forthcoming road season and next Summer should be on the champion's heels.
Burt (S.W.C.) was second, Len Fletcher, of ours, third. Our other man, Fred Bentley, found the distance a bit too short for his liking, but did well to finish fifth.
